title: Career roadmap · Genomics Lab Analyst
summary: A practical route from a B.Sc in Medical Biotechnology / Molecular Biology / Genomics into genomic laboratory analysis, molecular diagnostics, sequencing, bioinformatics, and biomedical research.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc route. If the student follows a 4-year honours pathway, use the additional year for advanced molecular techniques, NGS workflows, bioinformatics, clinical genomics, research internships and a dissertation.

about.label: Course alignment
about.text: Genomics Lab Analyst is directly aligned with the Medical Biotechnology / Molecular Biology / Genomics pathway.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry, laboratory and bioinformatics fundamentals; target Genomics Lab Analyst, Molecular Biology Assistant and Genomics Technician roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Develop expertise in NGS, variant analysis, clinical genomics, cancer genomics, population genomics or bioinformatics.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Genomics Analyst, Bioinformatics Analyst, Molecular Diagnostics Specialist or Research Associate roles.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine genomics with AI/ML, precision medicine, multi-omics, clinical interpretation, genomic data security and advanced diagnostics.

rows.text: Cell biology, genetics, biochemistry and laboratory safety

NGS data processing, sequence alignment, variant analysis and databases

Clinical/research genomics project, quality control and internship
Produce a reproducible genomics report from raw/public sequencing data

blocks.label: 4-year honours variant
blocks.text: Use Year 4 for NGS pipelines, clinical variant interpretation, advanced bioinformatics, multi-omics, research publication/dissertation work and a longer genomics internship.

PhD routes
Potential research directions include:
2040–2046 relevance

Genomics will increasingly combine high-throughput sequencing + computational biology + AI + precision medicine. Long-term relevance will require both biological understanding and computational capability, particularly in variant interpretation, multi-omics, clinical decision support, genomic data quality and responsible handling of sensitive genomic information.
